label: copy-phase input j in long (L>=8) sequences
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase (t > L). It never fires on original-phase or <DEL> steps, and never on the first copy step. It is almost entirely confined to long sequences: L=9 holds 79% of the mass, L=8 16%, and L<=5 has none. Within those sequences the rate peaks at recall_idx 2-3 and again at the last two steps (recall_idx 7-8). The strongest token cue is the fed-back input j (10x lift, 43% of the mass); 2 and n follow far behind. The top activations are nearly all j inputs near the end of L=9 sequences. Copy phase with L>=8 alone covers 95% of the mass but has only 5% precision. Adding input j gives 43% precision but only 27% recall, so most activations depend on hidden-state context that this predicate does not capture.
